item.title: Sen. Rick Scott Visits Israel, Meets with Israeli Leadership
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: U.S. Senator Rick Scott, a Florida Republican who serves on the Senate Armed Services and Foreign Relations committees, traveled to Israel this week to reaffirm U.S. support for the country and discuss bilateral cooperation, according to a statement from his office released today. During the visit, Scott met with Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon…
item.content:encoded:
U.S. Senator Rick Scott, a Florida Republican who serves on the Senate Armed Services and Foreign Relations committees, traveled to Israel this week to reaffirm U.S. support for the country and discuss bilateral cooperation, according to a statement from his office released today.

During the visit, Scott met with Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar, Israeli Defense Forces members, and U.S. military personnel stationed there. He traveled to the Golan Heights and Israel's Northern Command, where he received briefings on military operations in southern Lebanon. Scott also met with the mayor of Majdal Shams and members of the Druze community affected by a 2024 Hezbollah attack on a soccer field that killed 12 children.

Scott emphasized the strategic value of the U.S.-Israel partnership, highlighting collaboration on border security, defense technology, healthcare, and medicine production. "Israel is the good guy," Scott said in a statement, adding that the alliance represents the model for how "America First alliances should operate."

This marks Scott's seventh trip to Israel since his election as Florida governor in 2010. The visit comes after recent trips by the senator to Cyprus and Greece to discuss NATO security and Mediterranean collective defense.

The new consolidated MARC will operate at the Destin-Fort Walton Rigdon Center, located at the former NWF Fairgrounds. Two existing locations are closing: the…
item.content:encoded:
Okaloosa County is consolidating its Multi-Agency Resource Centers (MARCs) at a single new location beginning Monday, October 26 at 1 p.m., according to a press release from the county.

The new consolidated MARC will operate at the Destin-Fort Walton Rigdon Center, located at the former NWF Fairgrounds. Two existing locations are closing: the Crestview Community Center closes at the end of business Thursday, October 22, and the Destin-Fort Walton Beach Convention Center closes at the end of business Saturday, October 24.

County officials say residents seeking assistance should bring identification, proof of residence, insurance information, and other documentation related to disaster-related losses to ensure they receive appropriate aid. The resource centers have been helping residents navigate recovery and relief resources following recent disasters in the region.

item.title: FPL Offers Qualifying Hurricane Victims Up to $3,200 in Financial Assistance
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Some Florida Power & Light customers recovering from Hurricane Isaias could qualify for as much as $3,200 in combined assistance for electric bills and repairs to damaged electrical equipment. FPL has expanded assistance through its Saving Steps and Care To Share programs following the hurricane. Saving Steps is…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Some Florida Power & Light customers recovering from Hurricane Isaias could qualify for as much as $3,200 in combined assistance for electric bills and repairs to damaged electrical equipment.

FPL has expanded assistance through its Saving Steps and Care To Share programs following the hurricane.

Saving Steps is providing a $200 bill credit to nearly 10,000 previously income-qualified customers in areas affected by Isaias.

The program uses broader income eligibility than many traditional government assistance programs. Eligibility varies based on household size, income, county and the specific program.

FPL says Care To Share can provide qualifying customers with up to $2,000 for repairs to customer-owned electrical equipment damaged by the storm.

That can include equipment such as meter boxes and weatherheads that must be repaired before a home can safely receive electricity.

Care To Share can also provide up to $1,000 toward qualifying customers' electric bills.

Combined with the Saving Steps credit, assistance could total as much as $3,200 for some households.

FPL says the goal is to help customers with expenses that remain after the utility completes repairs to its own electrical system.

Customers have to meet eligibility requirements and should apply through FPL's assistance programs.

item.title: Escambia School Board Approves Additional Book Removals After Lengthy Public Opposition
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Escambia County School Board members unanimously approved another round of book removals Tuesday night, one day after a federal appeals court ruled board members can be required to testify about earlier decisions to remove books from district libraries. The board voted 4-0 to approve Superintendent Keith Leonard's…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Escambia County School Board members unanimously approved another round of book removals Tuesday night, one day after a federal appeals court ruled board members can be required to testify about earlier decisions to remove books from district libraries.

The board voted 4-0 to approve Superintendent Keith Leonard's recommendation to remove titles covered by the district's June 2025 directive concerning books appearing on the Florida Department of Education's book-removal list.

The action removes affected titles from district media centers, classroom libraries and recommended-reading lists.

The vote followed lengthy public comment from residents, parents and school media specialists both supporting and opposing the district's book policies.

Opponents cited titles including "Harriet the Spy," "Roll of Thunder, Hear My Cry," "Roots" and "Are You There God? It's Me, Margaret?" while arguing books should be evaluated individually.

One district media specialist told the board that parents already have the ability to limit what their children can check out or prevent their children from accessing school libraries altogether.

Parent Kristen Moschel also argued individual families should decide which books their children read.

Board members did not discuss the removal recommendation among themselves before voting unanimously to approve it.

The meeting came one day after the 11th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals upheld a lower-court decision requiring School Board members to sit for depositions in an ongoing federal lawsuit over previous book removals.

Board members had argued legislative privilege protected them from being compelled to testify about their decisions.

The appeals court concluded that the specific book-removal votes at issue involved applying existing School Board policies and were administrative rather than legislative acts.

The ruling does not decide the underlying lawsuit over whether the district's book removals violated the First Amendment.

item.title: Highway 182 resurfacing project starts Monday in Santa Rosa County
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Drivers heading through Santa Rosa County should plan for delays starting next week. Beginning Monday, October 26, work crews will begin a major resurfacing and widening project on Highway 182 between Chumuckla Highway and Allison Creek Lane, according to Santa Rosa County Communications. The project is expected to run through October 2027,…
item.content:encoded:
Drivers heading through Santa Rosa County should plan for delays starting next week. Beginning Monday, October 26, work crews will begin a major resurfacing and widening project on Highway 182 between Chumuckla Highway and Allison Creek Lane, according to Santa Rosa County Communications.

The project is expected to run through October 2027, weather permitting. Work will take place between 7 a.m. and 5 p.m. weekdays, and Highway 182 will be reduced to a single lane during paving operations. Santa Rosa County officials warn motorists to expect heavy delays, use caution in the work zone, and follow directions from flaggers and posted traffic control signs.

The improvements will include milling and resurfacing the roadway, replacing and upgrading culverts, re-establishing ditches, widening shoulders with rumble strips, adding pavement striping, and installing raised reflective pavement markers. More details and maps of the project area are available on the Santa Rosa County website.

item.title: Baldwin County Sees Spike in Bat Bites; Thomas Hospital Treats Six
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Thomas Hospital in Baldwin County, Alabama, has treated six patients for bat bites as the region experiences a rise in incidents, according to WKRG-TV 5. The uptick in bat-related injuries has raised concerns about potential rabies exposure, a serious public health risk. Health officials typically recommend immediate medical attention and…
item.content:encoded:
Thomas Hospital in Baldwin County, Alabama, has treated six patients for bat bites as the region experiences a rise in incidents, according to WKRG-TV 5.

The uptick in bat-related injuries has raised concerns about potential rabies exposure, a serious public health risk. Health officials typically recommend immediate medical attention and post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) vaccination for anyone bitten by a bat, since rabies is nearly always fatal once symptoms appear.

Bat bites can occur when the animals enter homes or come into contact with people outdoors. Experts advise residents to avoid handling bats directly and to seek medical care promptly if exposure occurs. Anyone who suspects contact with a bat should contact local health authorities or visit an emergency room.

item.title: Florida Executes Man Convicted in 1986 Deputy Killing
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: William Reaves, 77, was executed by lethal injection Tuesday evening at Florida State Prison for the 1986 murder of Indian River County Sheriff's Deputy Richard "Raz" Raczkowski. According to the Florida Department of Corrections, Reaves was pronounced dead at 6:12 p.m. The case dates back four decades. Reaves had been convicted in connection with…
item.content:encoded:
William Reaves, 77, was executed by lethal injection Tuesday evening at Florida State Prison for the 1986 murder of Indian River County Sheriff's Deputy Richard "Raz" Raczkowski. According to the Florida Department of Corrections, Reaves was pronounced dead at 6:12 p.m.

The case dates back four decades. Reaves had been convicted in connection with Raczkowski's death and had spent decades on Florida's death row before the execution was carried out.

This execution marks another capital punishment case in Florida, which maintains one of the nation's most active death row populations.

item.title: Escambia County Clears 330K Cubic Yards of Hurricane Isaias Debris; Over 1M Remain
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County crews and contracted haulers are working around the clock to clear storm debris left behind by Hurricane Isaias, with removal efforts ramped up to seven days a week since October 12. According to North Escambia, county-hired contractors have hauled away approximately 330,000 cubic yards of debris across more than 7,400 loads so…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County crews and contracted haulers are working around the clock to clear storm debris left behind by Hurricane Isaias, with removal efforts ramped up to seven days a week since October 12.

According to North Escambia, county-hired contractors have hauled away approximately 330,000 cubic yards of debris across more than 7,400 loads so far. Despite the aggressive pace, more than a million cubic yards of storm waste remain to be collected across the county.

The combined effort of county personnel and outside contractors reflects the scale of cleanup needed following the hurricane. Residents can expect continued collection activity throughout the county as crews work to clear remaining debris from residential and commercial areas.

item.content:encoded:
An Escambia County man is being held without bond following a drug-related search warrant that uncovered illegal narcotics, firearms, and body armor, according to the Escambia County Sheriff's Office.

The Sheriff's Narcotics Unit served the search warrant at a residence in the 200 block of East Ten Mile Road. Investigators recovered drugs, weapons, and body armor during the operation, though specific quantities and charges were not immediately detailed.

The suspect is in custody at the Escambia County jail pending further processing and formal charges. The investigation is ongoing, according to the Sheriff's Office.

item.content:encoded:
A $5.3 million road improvement project is now underway on West Highway 4, with crews beginning work Monday on the full 13-mile stretch from Highway 97 in Davisville to North Century Boulevard in Century, according to Escambia County.

The resurfacing effort represents a significant investment in the North Escambia corridor, which serves both local residents and through traffic between the two communities. Work has already started just east of Highway 97, and county officials expect the project to wrap up by spring 2027, weather permitting.

Drivers in the area should expect construction activity and possible traffic adjustments as the work progresses over the coming months. Escambia County said construction coordination could also affect the timeline, so commuters are advised to plan accordingly.

item.title: Florida courts reject GOP bids to block Democratic ads about Hope Florida scandal
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Florida courts have turned down two separate Republican attempts to stop the Florida Democratic Party from airing ads about the Hope Florida scandal, according to a statement from the Democratic Party Tuesday. A Highlands County circuit judge denied the Republican Party of Florida's emergency request to pull the ads off the air without a hearing.…
item.content:encoded:
Florida courts have turned down two separate Republican attempts to stop the Florida Democratic Party from airing ads about the Hope Florida scandal, according to a statement from the Democratic Party Tuesday.

A Highlands County circuit judge denied the Republican Party of Florida's emergency request to pull the ads off the air without a hearing. That ruling follows an earlier decision by the First District Court of Appeal on October 16 to reject a bid by Attorney General James Uthmeier and other officials to ban publication of grand jury findings related to Hope Florida.

Florida Democratic Party Chair Nikki Fried said the repeated legal losses show Republicans are trying to suppress information ahead of the election. "Floridians deserve sunlight," Fried said in a statement. "Our ads are staying on the air, and we will keep telling voters exactly what happened."

The appeals court has also ordered officials named in the case to explain what they know about how a redacted version of the grand jury report became public. Court records in both Hope Florida cases are set to be addressed in motions due around October 25 and 26.

item.title: Six bat bite cases reported at Alabama hospital; rabies concerns prompt warnings
item.dc:creator: newsroom

Emergency department physicians at the hospital say the cluster is notable for occurring over such a compressed timeframe. While bat encounters happen…
item.content:encoded:
Thomas Hospital in Baldwin County, Alabama, has treated at least six patients for bat bites or exposure in the past week, marking an unusual surge in such cases, according to WKRG News 5.

Emergency department physicians at the hospital say the cluster is notable for occurring over such a compressed timeframe. While bat encounters happen occasionally, multiple exposures in days typically warrant closer investigation and public health attention.

Rabies is a serious concern with bat bites, as the virus can be transmitted through saliva. Health officials generally recommend that anyone bitten by a bat seek immediate medical attention and post-exposure prophylaxis if warranted. The hospital's treatment of multiple cases suggests local residents may be encountering bats at higher-than-usual rates, possibly due to seasonal migration or habitat changes.

No additional details on patient conditions or the circumstances of the exposures were immediately available.

item.title: Florida reports nearly 60% drop in fentanyl deaths since 2023
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Florida has recorded a dramatic decline in fentanyl-related deaths, with new data showing nearly 3,000 fewer deaths annually compared to 2023 levels, according to a report from the Florida Medical Examiners Commission released Tuesday by Governor Ron DeSantis's office. Fentanyl deaths fell from roughly 5,000 in 2023 to approximately 2,000 by…
item.content:encoded:
Florida has recorded a dramatic decline in fentanyl-related deaths, with new data showing nearly 3,000 fewer deaths annually compared to 2023 levels, according to a report from the Florida Medical Examiners Commission released Tuesday by Governor Ron DeSantis's office.

Fentanyl deaths fell from roughly 5,000 in 2023 to approximately 2,000 by 2025—a nearly 60% reduction. From 2024 to 2025 alone, fentanyl-caused deaths dropped 37%, while deaths from fentanyl analogs declined by more than 50%. The state also saw broader declines across other drug-related deaths: opioid-caused deaths fell 33%, cocaine deaths dropped 16%, and methamphetamine deaths decreased 23%.

The governor attributed much of the progress to the State Assistance for Fentanyl Eradication (S.A.F.E.) grant program, established in 2023 to fund large-scale drug investigations and support local law enforcement. Since its launch, the program has yielded nearly 3,000 arrests of drug traffickers and dealers, along with significant seizures: more than 600 pounds of fentanyl, over 65,000 fentanyl pills, nearly 800 pounds of cocaine, more than 520 pounds of methamphetamine, and more than $6.6 million in cash. Law enforcement also recovered nearly 1,000 firearms and 90 vehicles.

Recent operations funded through S.A.F.E. include October's Operation Ice Breaker, which charged 25 individuals following a South Florida trafficking investigation that netted over 100 pounds of cocaine and 16 firearms, and September's Operation End of Worlds, which dismantled a major Polk County fentanyl and methamphetamine organization, resulting in 39 arrests.

item.title: Navarre Library Reopens Wednesday After Hurricane Closure

The Jay, Pace, and Gulf Breeze libraries and Library Administration remain open to serve the community. However, Milton Library and the Family…
item.content:encoded:
The Santa Rosa County Library System will reopen the Navarre Library on Wednesday, October 21, during regular operating hours, marking a step forward in the county's recovery from the recent hurricane.

The Jay, Pace, and Gulf Breeze libraries and Library Administration remain open to serve the community. However, Milton Library and the Family History & Research Center will stay closed until further notice as cleanup and repairs continue.

To support residents navigating recovery, open Santa Rosa County libraries are providing additional computers for public use. The computers will help community members access recovery information, complete online forms, and connect with assistance programs. The library system encourages residents to call (850) 981-7323 or visit www.santarosa.fl.gov/libraries for updates on remaining closures and additional reopening timelines.

item.title: Florida Notifying Drivers After License and Vehicle Records Exposed in Data Breach
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: TALLAHASSEE, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Florida motorists are being notified after an unauthorized intruder gained access to records maintained by the Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles. FLHSMV says the incident happened Sept. 4 when a malicious actor using compromised credentials accessed department systems. Information…
item.content:encoded:
TALLAHASSEE, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Florida motorists are being notified after an unauthorized intruder gained access to records maintained by the Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles.


FLHSMV says the incident happened Sept. 4 when a malicious actor using compromised credentials accessed department systems.


Information potentially affected includes driver's license and motor-vehicle data, document images and other personal information maintained by the department.


The state has not publicly disclosed how many Floridians were affected.


FLHSMV says it has found no evidence so far that the exposed information has been misused.

Notification letters are being mailed this week to current driver's license and identification-card holders whose information may have been compromised.


Those individuals are being offered one year of free credit and identity monitoring through Sontiq, a TransUnion company. The protection also includes $1 million in identity-theft insurance.


The state is also issuing a broader public notice because it may no longer have current addresses for some affected people who previously held a Florida driver's license, identification card or vehicle title.


FLHSMV is encouraging potentially affected Floridians to review account statements and credit reports, monitor financial and online accounts and consider placing a fraud alert or security freeze with the major credit bureaus.


People who previously held Florida licenses, identification cards or vehicle titles and don't receive a mailed notice can contact FLHSMV to determine whether they were affected.
